A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 15-page versions of the same Think&Cite work. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices can be matched despite local revisions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Think&Cite evaluations on ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5, including benchmark results, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds computational-cost measurements and associated citation results in Appendix B, Table 4.

M1.justification: Equation (3) drops historical context H from the stated query-reformulation inputs, while Equation (4) retains it for sentence generation. This is a limited change to the specified inputs; the SG-MCTS framework and reward construction remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5 tasks using Wikipedia and Sphere. The added computational analysis uses existing ASQA coverage; no dataset, domain, population, or distinct task scenario is added.

E2.justification: FG-Reward and VTG, already accuracy baselines in v1, participate in the new computational-cost comparison in v2 Table 4. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark, ablation, and sensitivity experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds average per-question inference time and generated-token measurements on ASQA with GPT-4o. Its 10/20/30/40-iteration budgets already appeared in Figure 3. Existing benchmark metrics, data settings, and policy/reward models remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a computational-expense analysis relating search budgets, inference costs, and citation quality, with baseline comparisons. The existing component ablations, reflection and hyperparameter sweeps, and qualitative ASQA case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new average time and token measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds time/token results, including 96 seconds and 1,547 tokens per question at 30 iterations, plus separate citation recall/precision entries across budgets. Tables 1–2 and the existing plotted performance results are unchanged; this is additional reporting, not a demonstrated improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Equation (3) revises the formal query-update dependency by removing H. The sentence-level MDP, maximum-entropy/DPO derivation, reward formulas, UCT, and backpropagation mathematics otherwise remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim tree-search-based attributed generation, reflection-guided MCTS, generation/attribution progress rewards, and superiority over the evaluated baselines on three datasets. Terminology changes and additional cost evidence do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B interprets the cost-quality relationship through test-time scaling and explains FG-Reward and VTG costs through rejection sampling and corpus-wide verification. The existing limitations concerning computational expense, dataset coverage, and alternative search algorithms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a dataset/source-code availability link and explicitly states inference without fine-tuning. Section 5.1 now specifies the ten-step reflection cap, already used in v1's sensitivity analysis, and Appendix B supplies inference-cost information. These disclosures do not establish changed execution settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for Lewis et al. (2020), Self-RAG, and Narayan et al. (2023), while removing Cobbe et al. (2021), Dai et al. (2024), and Silver et al. (2017). This locally expands positioning around retrieval, tree decoding, and generation blueprints.

P1.justification: Local edits standardize 'Progress Reward Modeling' and 'MCTS iterations,' clarify sentence-level nodes, output assembly, and stopping, and add acknowledgments and a computational-cost appendix. The main section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds computational-cost Table 4 and changes Figure 3's simulation-axis terminology and caption to iterations. Appendix content reflows, and prompt Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7. Existing benchmark and ablation table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B/Table 4 provides useful quantitative evidence about computational costs that v1 discussed qualitatively. Clearer method documentation and the stated dataset/code access also improve transparency. The gains are limited: core empirical evidence is unchanged, timing measurements lack hardware and repeated-run details, and Equation (3)'s removal of H is unexplained.
